gloss: deficit; in the red; red ink

definitions.explanation: A financial situation where expenses exceed income or losses exceed gains.
Text written or printed in red ink, often for corrections or emphasis.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今月|こんげつ}→今月：00720_kongetsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{赤字|あかじ}⟦だった→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: This month was in the red.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧３⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧⟦{連続|れんぞく}→連続：03783_renzoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{赤字|あかじ}⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: The company has been in deficit for three consecutive years.

examples.japanese: ⟦{家計|かけい}→家計：12287_kakei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{赤字|あかじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ならないように→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦{毎月|まいつき}→毎月：00732_maitsuki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{支出|ししゅつ}→支出：03169_shishutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見直|みなお}している→見直す：04579_minaosu⟧。
examples.english: I review my monthly expenses so the household budget doesn't go into the red.

examples.japanese: {赤字|あかじ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{直|なお}す→直す：00869_naosu⟧。
⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{作文|さくぶん}→作文：02884_sakubun⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{赤字|あかじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れた→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: The teacher put red corrections on the essay.

examples.japanese: ⟦{原稿|げんこう}→原稿：00064_genkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{赤字|あかじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦{入|はい}っていた→入る：00494_hairu⟧⟦ので→ので：09501_node⟧、⟦{書|か}き{直|なお}す→書き直す：04597_kakinaosu⟧⟦ことにした→ことにする：10986_kotonisuru⟧。
examples.english: There were so many red corrections in the manuscript that I decided to rewrite it.

notes:
{赤字|あかじ} literally means 'red letters', from the practice of recording losses in red ink.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {赤字|あかじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to go into the red)
- {赤字|あかじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ (to incur a loss)
- {赤字|あかじ}⟦{経営|けいえい}→経営：02740_keiei⟧ (operating at a loss)
- {赤字|あかじ}⟦{国債|こくさい}→国債：12016_kokusai⟧ (deficit-covering bonds)
- ⟦{財政|ざいせい}→財政：05757_zaisei⟧{赤字|あかじ} (fiscal deficit)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {赤字|あかじ} (deficit, in the red)
- ⟦{黒字|くろじ}→黒字：04715_kuroji⟧ (surplus, in the black)

USAGE:
In Japanese accounting, losses traditionally were written in red (⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧), while profits were in black (⟦{黒|くろ}→黒：02205_kuro⟧), similar to Western conventions.
